title: Revalidation evidence — the value of pkit::analysis:revalidation-evidence, version 1
description: The data point's companion schema (COR-052 point 5; software-analysis DEC-001 point 7): executed results that confirm or refute an analysis artefact at a commit — a test run against a use case, a trace through a journey. This capability runs nothing: the results arrive from a capability that runs them, or from the project's own filler file. One entry per artefact and commit, keyed by the pair: its `id` is `<artefact>@<commit>`. The point is `union`, no default takes part, and its inert policy is `fallback`, because the evidence advises: a revalidation record cites it as support for an artefact's outcome and never in place of one, and only a revalidation or a deferral recorded on the artefact clears friction (COR-050). The ids' shapes are `analysis.schema.json`'s, their one home. The version rises only on a change that breaks existing fillers.

evidence.description: The result of one executed check, for one artefact at one commit.

id.description: The entry's key, the pair it is for: `<artefact>@<commit>`, the two fields below. A revalidation record cites the entry by it.

artefact.description: The artefact the run confirms or refutes.

commit.description: The commit the run was made against: the version of the system the result is true of.

result.description: `passed`: the run did what the artefact describes — support for `holds`. `failed`: it did not — a regression with proof attached, or a sign the analysis is stale; the revalidation decides which (DEC-001 points 5 and 7).

ran.description: What was run, so a person can find it and run it again: a test by its name (`tests/test_run.py::test_sandbox`), a trace, a scripted walk through a journey.

steps.description: The steps and variants the run went through, by their numbers and letters (`2`, `2a`). They are cited, which is why they are never renumbered (DEC-001 point 3).

where.description: Where the result can be read: a pipeline run, a report file.

by.description: Who or what ran it: a capability, a pipeline, a person.
